subject: Azure Marketplace: annual listing fee & partner program renewal
messages:
From: Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@microsoft.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Azure Marketplace Billing <marketplace-billing@microsoft.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure Marketplace annual listing fee & partner program renewal

Hi Karthik and Marissa,

Hope you’re both well. Quick note to flag upcoming changes to the Azure Marketplace partner terms that will affect listing economics starting July 1. The partner team released a fee update that increases the standard marketplace listing/commission from 3% to 6% for new renewals unless partners elect into a revised co-sell tier.

Two items for Redwood:
- Fee impact: preliminary summary attached (2026_fee_summary.xlsx).
- Program change: partner tiers are being restructured; some benefits (co-sell credits, elevated listing placement) are gated behind higher revenue thresholds (see azure_partner_changes.pdf).

We know this can materially affect ISV GTM plans. Would Redwood be open to a short call next week so we can walk the proposal and see whether an alternative carve-out or rebate structure is possible given your marketplace performance and committed roadmap? I can pull in billing and partner ops if that’s helpful.

Proposed slots: Thu 6/4 10:00–11:00 PT, Mon 6/8 8:30–9:00 PT.

Regards,
Jane Sullivan
Partner Manager, Azure Marketplace
Microsoft Corporation

Attachments: 2026_fee_summary.xlsx, azure_partner_changes.pdf

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@microsoft.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace annual listing fee & partner program renewal

Thanks for the heads up, Jane — we appreciate the proactive reach.

On Wed, Jun 3, 2026 at 9:12 AM Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@microsoft.com> wrote:
> Hi Karthik and Marissa,
> 
> Hope you’re both well. Quick note to flag upcoming changes to the Azure Marketplace partner terms...

Marissa, Laura, Neha — looping you all in. Short term ask: can someone run a quick top-line impact on our active listings (Q2 bookings tied to marketplace) and any committed customer renewals that could be exposed if the fee reset applies July 1? We need a position before the call with Jane.

Jane — we can take Thu 6/4 10:00 PT. If marketplace billing needs to be on, please include them. Goal for the call: understand options (rebate, grandfathering existing renewals, tier exception) and outline a mutual action plan.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Partnerships (Sales)
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Jun 2026 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Azure Marketplace annual listing fee & partner program renewal — quick impact snapshot

Putting together a short impact deck and a numbers sheet (attached: redwood_impact_az_q3.xlsx). Quick notes from the first pass:
- Estimated ARR through marketplace (tied to listings subject to fee) = $1.8M annualized.
- If fee moves to 6% with no rebate, incremental annual cost (to customer-facing pricing/margins) ~ $32k in marketplace commissions (we ultimately absorb some; others get passed to customers).
- Several key renewals between July–Sep reside in enterprise accounts where marketplace purchasing is preferred — those are the negotiable levers.

Recommend we ask for either:
1) grandfathering existing renewal contracts until next contract year, or
2) a 12-month rebate/credit of the delta to net us back to ~3% effective fee, tied to committed marketplace spend.

I’ll have a short deck for the call Thu 6/10 if we push to that slot.

—Marissa
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_impact_az_q3.xlsx

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@microsoft.com>, marketplace-billing@microsoft.com
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace annual listing fee & partner program renewal — Redwood position

Hi Jane,

Thanks for hosting time on short notice today and for the materials. After internal review, Redwood’s position is as follows:

1) We recognize Microsoft’s desire to re-align marketplace economics, but a full increase to 6% without transition would materially impact our go-to-market and introduce margin pressure for renewals where customers require marketplace purchasing.
2) Given Redwood’s volume and multi-region roadmap (we’re expanding private deployments and dedicated capacity offers where customers often route via Azure), we believe a bespoke transition makes sense.

Proposal (counter):
- Keep effective marketplace fee at ~3% for existing contracts that renew before 2027, or provide a rebate to offset the delta for 12 months tied to committed marketplace revenue (proposal_REDWOOD_rebate_v1.pdf attached).
- In exchange, Redwood will commit to a co-marketing package (three joint webinars + co-sell introduction packets) and a 9-month runway to transition new listings to the new tier.

Please confirm whether marketplace-billing can consider a temporary rebate mechanism or whether we should pursue a partner-tier upgrade track to achieve comparable economics. If useful, here is the mutual action plan link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/REDWOOD-2026-AZ-0043 (contains proposed milestones and timelines).

Laura Bennett
SVP, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposal_REDWOOD_rebate_v1.pdf

From: Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@microsoft.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: marketplace-billing@microsoft.com, CloudPartnerOps <cpops@cloudsolutionsinc.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace annual listing fee & partner program renewal — Microsoft response

Laura / Karthik — thanks for the clear counter. I took your proposal to billing and partner ops. Summary of Microsoft’s offer: 

1) Transitional compromise: effective fee for your existing catalog renewals will be set at 4% for a 12-month period (retroactive to July 1 for renewals processed in that window).
2) Additionally, Microsoft can provide a one-time marketplace rebate equal to the delta between 4% and 3% for confirmed committed marketplace spend of $250k+ within the next 12 months (rebate instrument will be issued as marketplace credits).
3) Path to tier upgrade: if Redwood meets defined co-sell activity thresholds (outlined separately by CloudPartnerOps), we’ll consider upgrading you to the higher partner tier which carries reduced effective placement fees and priority GTM support.

We’ll follow up with formal paperwork from billing. For next steps, if Redwood accepts in principle, we’ll draft the mutual action plan and rebate instrument and route for signature.

Happy to jump on a follow-up if you want to negotiate the rebate threshold or timing.

Best,
Jane Sullivan
Partner Manager, Azure Marketplace
Microsoft Corporation

Attachments: microsoft_transitional_offer_2026.pdf
